title: Competing Chern states revealed by quasiparticle charging in moiré rhombohedral graphene
authors: Hongyuan Li, Zuhan Geng, Junseok Seo, Chenxi Xu, Yifan Jiang, Shenyong Ye, Zhenqi Hua, Jiabin Xie, Lujin Min, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Yasuda, Xiaomeng Liu, Long Ju, Jie Shan, Kin Fai Mak
abstract: Moiré materials realize a versatile platform for exploring the physics of fractional Chern insulators (FCIs). The recently observed evolution from FCIs to an extended quantum anomalous Hall background upon lowering the electronic temperature in moiré rhombohedral graphene (mRG)8 raises a fundamental question: Is it caused by a failure to equilibrate the edge states of an FCI or by a genuine phase transition in the bulk from an FCI to a generalized anomalous Hall crystal? Here we address this question by probing quasiparticle charging in a mesoscopic mRG antidot device and by bulk resistance measurements, both of which are bulk-sensitive and free from complications from edge states. Tunneling to the mRG antidot reveals quasiparticles carrying one electron charge for both Chern states at filling factors ν=1 and 2/3 at low temperatures. Temperature dependence measurements of the bulk resistance near ν=2/3 further suggest a thermodynamic phase transition from an FCI to a generalized anomalous Hall crystal at temperatures below about 150mK. The results clearly exclude the edge state equilibration scenario and favor the phase transition scenario. Our work establishes mesoscopic probes as a powerful approach to uncover competing ground states in moiré materials and provides a basis for probing fractionalized excitations in FCIs.
summary: The researchers investigated the nature of a phase change in moiré rhombohedral graphene between two topological states: an FCI and an anomalous Hall crystal. By using bulk-sensitive quasiparticle charging measurements, they definitively ruled out edge effects and established that the transition is a genuine thermodynamic phase transition occurring at very low temperatures.
main_problem: The study aims to resolve whether the observed transition from a Fractional Chern Insulator (FCI) to an extended quantum anomalous Hall background in moiré rhombohedral graphene is due to edge state equilibration failure or a genuine bulk phase transition.
main_result: Quasiparticle charging measurements and temperature-dependent bulk resistance strongly suggest that the system undergoes a thermodynamic phase transition from an FCI to a generalized anomalous Hall crystal at low temperatures, ruling out the edge state scenario.
method: The research employs mesoscopic transport measurements, including quasiparticle tunneling spectroscopy (measuring diagonal resistance) and bulk longitudinal/Hall resistance mapping across varying filling factors and temperatures.
model_or_system: The physical system is moiré rhombohedral graphene (mRG), fabricated into a mesoscopic antidot device structure. The physics explores competing topological ground states, specifically FCI versus generalized anomalous Hall crystal phases.
key_observables:
Quasiparticle charge carried during tunneling ($e^*$), quantized resistance plateaus ($R_{xx}, R_{xy}$), and the temperature dependence of bulk resistance near critical filling factors ($
u=2/3$).
important_parameters: Low temperatures (down to 12 mK) are crucial for observing clear signatures; the transition occurs below $T \approx 150$ mK.
main_assumptions: The use of bulk-sensitive antidot measurements is necessary to overcome ambiguities inherent in edge-state dominated Hall bar measurements.
figures_summary:
Figures illustrate device schematics, resonant tunneling peaks (Coulomb oscillations) at specific fillings ($
u=1, 2/3$), and phase diagrams showing the competition between FCI and GAHC states as temperature changes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents evidence from quasiparticle charging measurements to establish charge quantization, followed by bulk resistance mapping that reveals a temperature-dependent transition between two distinct topological phases.
why_interesting: This work provides experimental confirmation of competing correlated ground states in moiré systems, which is highly relevant for understanding emergent topological order and fractionalized excitations in strongly interacting electron systems.
